liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Eleven** (3 reviews, 1 other source): An overlap in this performance was spliced together during the digital cleanup of the tape; The jam running from The Eleven into Caution is unusual and especially enjoyable [1][3][5][11]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): The band sounds like it is still warming up here, less forceful than the rest of the show; The Other One is powerful but still a developing improvisational vehicle for the band [3][11]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (2 reviews): The recording cuts off abruptly at the end of Cryptical, which seemed to have more to give; The only drawback is a tape cut at the end of Cryptical [5][7]
- **Caution (Do Not Step on Tracks)** (1 review): Caution is interrupted shortly after The Eleven grooves, probably by a reel change [10]

## The recordings

- **gd69-02-05.sbd.cotsman.8993.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 57 min; rated 4.07/5 by 30 [1]. Said about its sound: A solid recording for its era, though well short of perfect; The tape has some annoying interruptions but otherwise excellent quality [5][13]

## Around the show

- DeadBase X lists this date as Omaha, Nebraska, with a completely different setlist, contradicting this Kansas City attribution [13]
- Dark Star is solid improvisation but not yet as monstrous as versions later the same month [3]
- The show reflects a new direction, moving decisively past the primal Dead sound of 1968 [8]
- The Dark Star > St. Stephen > Eleven sequence anticipates what became Live Dead at the end of the month [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-02-05.sbd.cotsman.8993.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Chuck Gannon and J. Cotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Sound Forge was used to normalize levels, remove crackles and discontinuities, and splice an overlap in The Eleven [1]
